notes: Phase 10 review treats JBank as a narrow exception to CYA's normal DeFi deprioritization because the product has a historically significant staking/outcome change. First-party JBank material identifies a decentralized self-custody protocol launched by JuCoin and currently exposes staking plus lending/POL mechanics. A project-authored Ju.com community post dated 2025-11-04 documents Flexible, 180-day and 365-day staking with auto-compounding rewards every eight hours. JBank's own current site reproduces a dated 2025-12-04 notice for long-term staked assets: users choosing the International Version can wait six months for release or use performance-based accelerated unlocking, and static returns do not accrue during either waiting/unlocking route. This creates direct CYA relevance around changed return and access mechanics even though the underlying protocol is decentralized. Preserve self-custody/on-chain architecture rather than misclassifying it as a centralized deposit account. Do not convert JBank's 'guaranteed returns', high-APY, or predictable-return marketing into verified realized return or principal protection. The June 2025 JuCoin listing notice calls the JBank token JUC on JuChain, while later JBank materials use JUB; the exact JUC-to-JUB token migration/rename chronology remains unresolved and must be stated as uncertainty rather than silently harmonized. The reviewed sources do not establish that every long-term staker completed release after the six-month period, so customer outcome must remain unknown unless stronger evidence is found.
